approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It makes random atom, bond and ring edits, filters invalid and previously proposed molecules, and directly evaluates the first full batch that passes its short-term memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even if that neighbor is worse, while keeping a separate record of the best molecule found. After the selected move, it stores up to four signed local-motif changes that would reverse parts of that move. These restrictions last four completed steps, refresh on overlap and can be released in oldest-first order when they obstruct generation. At present, matching any single remembered inverse attribute vetoes a candidate, so a shared local feature can suppress a move without evidence that it reverses the rest of the remembered transition.
approach.novelty: Add a conjunction across the two inverse signs from the same remembered transition. A candidate is tabu only when it both removes at least one local motif introduced by that transition and restores at least one local motif that transition removed. A partial match remains admissible, and matches belonging to different transitions cannot be combined. This changes the meaning of a structural reversal without changing the underlying graph walk. The lineage currently contains only its root, which tested independent single-attribute vetoes; no sibling has tested this paired evidence rule. The experiment asks whether admitting partially overlapping moves exposes more useful neighbors while a smaller set of structurally supported vetoes continues to affect the walk.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-e1533ca81aec rejects a valid novel graph edit whenever any one changed signed local motif matches an active inverse restriction. Its confirmed observation reports 3,945 vetoes among 5,395 valid novel draws (73.1233%), while only 131 of 1,450 evaluated neighbors beat their current source (9.0345%) and their mean score difference was -0.082000. One batch needed 493 attempts and four oldest-entry releases. The actual summary.json and run.log establish successful completion and a single-replica macro Top-1 of 0.510812888963087, without a comparative control. A read-only reclassification of the recorded veto provenance finds that just 268 vetoes match both inverse signs from the same selected transition; the other 3,677 have only partial or cross-transition matches. Those partial matches occur in all 140 post-initial batches. Thus single-attribute matching imposes a broad restriction even when the move lacks the two-sided signature of reversing one remembered transition. The evidence establishes this selectivity limitation, but does not establish that relaxing it improves scores or chemistry.
hypothesis: Replace any-single-attribute tabu vetoes with same-transition bidirectional inverse-attribute matching: veto a valid novel graph edit only if its signed motif changes match at least one active positive restriction and at least one active negative restriction originating from the same selected accepted transition.

finding_summary.headline: Paired tabu matching reproduced; an identity lookup crash left one replica incomplete.
finding_summary.insights:
The narrower reversal test reproducibly changes oracle allocation and the walk while retaining active structural memory. Correct same-transition matching, intact four-step expiry and the surviving fresh-identity vetoes rule out erased memory as the source of easier admission. Most newly admitted neighbors still score below their source, so greater admissibility has not established better average neighborhood quality. The useful effects arise from a minority of admitted moves; the separate value of the remaining vetoes remains unmeasured because rejected alternatives were never scored.

The identity lookup failure previously seen only in the supplied smoke evidence now occurs in a formal replica. Its cause is localized: the generator keys pending proposals by a molecular spelling that changes when the evaluator canonicalizes it. The failing proposal was one of the newly admitted partial matches. This exposes an inherited execution limitation on the newly accessible trajectory and prevents a claim of complete or repeatable score benefit. A stable identity join and a complete replica are needed before assessing that benefit.

The molecular assessment shows that partial-overlap admission still explores recurring ring-rich families with unusual sulfur bonding, dense ring junctions and unspecified geometry. Memory selectivity does not establish chemically plausible alternatives or broad useful scaffold coverage; those limitations remain separate from the verified matching effect.
finding_summary.results:
Across the two added replicas' observed streams, the original any-match rule would veto 1,578 of 2,831 valid novel attempts (55.74%); the paired rule vetoed 121 (4.27%) on the same candidates and live memory. All 1,457 newly admitted proposals reached evaluation, accounting for 53.76% of optimizer evaluations. Of these, 141 beat their current source (9.68%), and their mean neighbor-minus-source score was -0.09247. They supplied 141 actual next-current states and 60 strict incumbent-improving observations. The remaining restrictions vetoed 112 distinct task/run molecular identities, changed 79 of 271 batches and produced nine selected next states absent from the passive unfiltered batch. Matching and memory-lifecycle checks agreed with the intended rule throughout the observed execution.

The first added replica completed all five tasks at 300 evaluations each, scoring 0.5277988 in macro final Top-1 versus 0.5180779 in the earlier screening replica of this same algorithm. The second added replica completed four tasks but crashed on zaleplon after 110 evaluations. Its completed final scores were 0.6092183 for decoration hopping, 0.9148144 for DRD2, 0.2018564 for median_2 and 0.4484554 for sitagliptin. The evaluator reports 1,310 total calls and no macro score for that replica, so there is no complete three-seed score estimate.

The crash occurred after the evaluator scored a full ten-molecule batch. The first accepted molecule's canonical spelling changed between generation and feedback, so its pending record could not be found. All ten evaluations are visible in the trajectory, but none of that batch's feedback was ingested and no next state was selected.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich neutral molecules range from recognizable aryl amides to dense sulfur cages with unusual bonding and unspecified geometry.
molecular.overall_character: Every listed objective has molecular observations. The first task has 410 evaluated molecules, including 390 optimizer proposals; its supplied trajectories end at evaluation 300 for seed 1 and 110 for seed 2. Each other task has 600 evaluated molecules and 580 optimizer proposals. The report describes only those observations. Every optimizer proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9872 for the first task, 1.0 for the next ring-rich families, and 0.719 for the final objective. These are text-based molecule-presence rates, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The molecules retain recognizable indole carboxamides, nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycles, aryl amines, esters and ethers, but often introduce unusual sulfur atoms into ring junctions or multiple bonds. Dense polycycles, bridged lactam-like systems, sulfur-nitrogen connections and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds occur alongside ordinary thiols and thioethers. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.1 to 70.2; the output is predominantly moderately sized to bulky multiring chemistry rather than tiny fragments or unbounded chains. Charged_rate is 0.0 throughout, which does not establish ordinary sulfur valence, synthetic accessibility or the absence of protonatable amines. Stereocentre_rate is also 0.0 throughout despite many substituted saturated centres and complex ring junctions. Chemical plausibility is mixed: conventional aryl amides are recognizable synthesis targets, whereas some sulfur-rich cages would require substantial evidence of feasible geometry and bonding before being called practical compounds. The useful high-score families remain concentrated even though the full trajectories contain numerous local topological variants. The supplied comparison trajectories are seed 0 of n-d88727c16484 itself; differences below are comparisons between runs, not evidence about activation of an algorithm change. Unobserved stable replacements or configurations have no established score benefit.

per_task.generated_character: The high tail consists mainly of neutral indole carboxanilides bearing ethoxy or methoxy, methyl and thiol substituents. Seed 2 also reaches related sulfur-substituted benzofuran carboxamides, often carrying chloromethyl or chlorohydroxymethyl groups. These are moderately sized aromatic structures with recognizable amide and heteroaromatic chemistry. The digest records aromatic_atom_rate 0.9872, ring_closure_rate 1.0, mean_smiles_length 45.1 and charged_rate 0.0. Later seed-1 structures often partially saturate the indole, introduce nitrogen-oxygen bonds, and replace the anilide ring with unusual oxygen/sulfur heterocycles containing very short closures. The prior seed-0 best, 0.3966634883331815, instead used a sulfur-containing unsaturated bicyclic aryl-ketone structure with fluorinated nitrogen decoration. The new leading amides are more recognizable chemically while occupying a similar reported score range. Coverage is limited to the supplied 410 molecules; the seed-2 final excerpt stops at evaluation 110.
liabilities: Aryl thiols can introduce oxidation and reactivity concerns; replacing the amide with a thioester changes both stability and donor/acceptor character.
Chloromethyl, chlorohydroxymethyl and sulfenamide-like substituents occur in the high or late families, adding reactive functionality to otherwise conventional cores.
Late examples contain unusual short heteroaromatic closures or cumulated bonds within rings. New saturated centres are not stereochemically specified.
missing_features: Broader chemically stable substitutions around the useful aromatic amide relationship are not established among the leaders; thiols, chlorinated alcohols and sulfur-nitrogen substituents become common local alternatives.
Independent high-scoring core families are sparsely represented relative to indole, azaindole and benzofuran carboxamide variants.
Controlled changes of saturation and ring connectivity that retain the useful arrangement are incomplete, particularly in later nitrogen-oxygen and short-closure heterocyclic structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273, while its corresponding methoxy-for-methyl analogue scores 0.3697260049130546. Changing the leading carboxanilide to the phenyl thioester gives 0.35659046617209134, and an aza-ring analogue scores 0.37487325032997193. These observations favour the retained compact indole/aryl-amide arrangement and a particular substitution pattern, rather than simply adding heteroatoms. Seed 2 reaches 0.3748218641899741 with a thiophenol-containing carboxanilide. The optimizer low-tail nitrogen-hydroxylated, partly saturated heterocyclic amide scores 0.030639811858172862, and its related rearranged structure scores 0.03531194062974934. Late benzofuran amides with pyridyl or aminoaryl groups score 0.3193611482176961 and 0.319362339985752; the final dearomatized ring variant scores 0.19926437414690307. Preserving ring markers alone does not preserve the favourable aromatic amide chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family is bulky and heterocycle-rich. A fused nitrogen dicarbonyl core carries fluoromethyl and methylthiomethyl nitrogen substituents, a branched polyunsaturated carbon chain, and a methylene-linked nitrogen/oxygen heterocycle with an acetal-like alkyl appendage. These structures combine ordinary carbonyls, ethers and thioethers with extensive substitution and flexible side chains. All optimizer proposals have aromatic and ring-closure text markers; mean_smiles_length is 67.6 and max_smiles_length 82. The full trajectory also contains enlarged imino/carbonyl nitrogen rings and strained aryl-alkyne or irregular sulfur-containing variants. The prior seed-0 best, 0.6161710037174721, was another heavily elaborated carbonyl/thione nitrogen heterocycle with halogenated aromatic and sulfur-containing appendages. The new upper family has different linkages and substituents but remains chemically large and locally concentrated.
liabilities: The leading molecules combine substantial size, flexible unsaturation, acetal-like groups and thioethers, creating stability and synthetic-complexity concerns that are not resolved by their scores.
Some near-leading variants introduce oxygen-sulfur bonds rather than ordinary ethers, and other trajectory families contain strained aromatic or enlarged conjugated nitrogen rings.
Extra bridging or sulfur substitution can markedly change whole-molecule connectivity without producing a more clearly useful chemical family.
missing_features: Simpler, independently different cores retaining the useful polar and heteroaromatic relationships are not established in the supplied high tail, which repeatedly elaborates one large connected family.
Stable alternatives to the polyene and acetal-like appendages are incompletely demonstrated. The score ties show tolerance of peripheral edits, not a uniquely required chain or sulfur group.
Defined alkene geometry and configuration at the substituted acetal-like centres are missing from the leading structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. Several elaborated seed-2 polyene/acetal relatives share the best value, 0.6092182584436399, despite changing terminal unsaturation, chlorinating an alkyl arm, shortening an alkoxy group or replacing an acetal oxygen substituent with sulfur. A close ether-connectivity variant ends at 0.6043732099581406. Earlier related structures retaining a benzyl aromatic appendage score 0.6012751220024138 and 0.5983687592684133. A further bridge between core and appendage scores 0.5756365894774199, and a sulfur-containing core rearrangement scores 0.5548207448659938. Optimizer low examples with contracted or rearranged versions of the starting carbonyl core score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063. The sampled gradient rewards a particular connected nitrogen/carbonyl/heteroaryl assembly with elaborated side chains, but does not sharply distinguish several peripheral chemical changes. Its plateau is below the prior seed-0 best.

per_task.generated_character: The high tail contains halogenated aromatic groups, phenols and accessible amino or aminomethyl groups attached to sulfur-rich partially saturated polycycles. Seed 2 connects a nitrogen-containing ring bearing a chlorinated aryl group to a fused sulfur/nitrogen framework. Seed 1 favours a more extensively bridged halogenated diaryl architecture with unusual multiply bonded sulfur. These are bulky ring-rich structures: ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 1.0, mean_smiles_length is 70.2 and halogen_rate is 0.9948. Formal charge markers are absent, but neutral SMILES still contain potentially protonatable amines. The unusual feature is sulfur at multiple ring junctions and in sulfur-sulfur or sulfur-carbon multiple bonds, not a lack of amine functionality. The prior seed-0 best, 0.8856242185485628, already combined aryl amines with unusual sulfur-containing linkers. The new upper structures are often more densely cyclized.
liabilities: Sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds, tetravalent ring sulfur and sulfur/nitrogen/cumulene-like connectivity are unusual medicinal motifs; zero formal charge does not establish that these frameworks are chemically stable or synthetically accessible.
The combination of extensive halogenation, multiple rings and amine-rich substituents creates an unresolved physicochemical and synthetic burden.
Some variants directly attach nitrogen to sulfur or introduce nitrogen-oxygen groups, changing the electronic character of otherwise useful amines.
missing_features: Ordinary saturated carbon/nitrogen/oxygen ring and linker alternatives preserving the useful amine/aromatic arrangement are not established among the supplied leaders; the high tail is dominated by unusual sulfur frameworks.
Functional-group placement is not reliably preserved during local edits: modifying the amine linkage or disrupting the terminal aromatic group can lose much of the observed score.
The dense ring junctions and substituted saturated centres lack defined stereochemistry, leaving the proposed molecular geometry incomplete.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminoaryl/sulfur-polycycle structure scores 0.9148143511682032. A close aminomethyl-for-methyl variant scores 0.8663008496126992, so adding another amine is not uniformly favourable. Related core carbon/sulfur substitutions share 0.8825461379136246, showing that some large electronic changes are not distinguished within that neighbourhood. Shortening the methylene connection between the central nitrogen and the sulfur-containing ring gives a late structure scoring 0.3331237338421948; replacing an aminomethyl group with an oxygen-nitrogen substituent gives 0.5308080684367313. Altering the terminal chlorinated aromatic ring into a sulfur-containing nonaromatic ring gives 0.04252669549740123. Early amido-acid/sulfonylated nitrogen structures score 0.007468397818197266 and 0.011568685009767434. The observed preference is for a particular accessible-amine, linker and aromatic arrangement over the initial acid/amide family. It does not establish that the unusual sulfur framework is the only way to realize those relationships.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 high family comprises large bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring systems containing lactam-like carbonyls, a hydrazine linkage, a phenylene ether region and an ester/methoxy-substituted aryl or pyridyl group. Saturated ring atoms and aromatic surfaces coexist, rather than the output being uniformly flat or ring-poor. Several leading structures contain only ordinary carbon, nitrogen and oxygen connectivity, although their complex topology makes synthesis nontrivial. Ring_closure_rate and aromatic_atom_rate are both 1.0; mean_smiles_length is 65.3 and max_smiles_length 77. Later and seed-1 families often introduce unusual ring sulfur, aryl hypobromites and brominated side chains. The prior seed-0 leader, 0.2107445781802027, was another bridged nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl structure. The new best retains that broad polycyclic polar character with a different ring arrangement and does not exceed its score.
liabilities: Large bridged frameworks and nitrogen-nitrogen linkages complicate synthesis and conformational interpretation even in the more conventional leading examples.
Other high or late variants contain tetravalent sulfur with nonstandard ring bonding, while low families carry aryl hypobromite and brominated sulfur-containing side chains.
Reactive peripheral groups and dense ring closures are not accompanied by evidence of chemical stability, accessible stereochemistry or improved properties.
missing_features: Independent, chemically ordinary scaffolds that retain the useful nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic arrangement are not established among the leading examples; the high tail is a concentrated bridged-ring family.

Coherent simplification and controlled changes of ring fusion are incompletely demonstrated. Ring opening can lose the useful organization, while adding unusual sulfur does not improve the cited matched score.
Configurationally specified ring junctions are missing despite the intricate saturated topology.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The bridged hydrazine/lactam-rich structure reaches 0.20185639717998205. A related azaaryl/ring-nitrogen analogue scores 0.1996542320706886, exactly the value of its unusual sulfur-for-nitrogen ring substitution. Thus the upper score does not require the introduced sulfur. Replacing a methoxy group with hydroxyl in the leading family gives 0.1960732916346388, and a different ring/carbonyl arrangement scores 0.1981349435950214. The optimizer low tail includes an opened carbonyl/hydrazide derivative at 0.12467972074136988 and a highly substituted sulfur/hypobromite molecule at 0.12870267321446027. Late sulfur-containing polycycles score 0.18257811736139357 and 0.1881666776148033, below the earlier neutral carbon/nitrogen/oxygen leader. The visible preference is for a coordinated multiring nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement; adding sulfur, halogen or further ring complexity is not a general improvement rule.

per_task.generated_character: The high seed-1 molecules are compact but exceptionally dense sulfur-rich polycycles. A nitrogen dicarbonyl heterocycle is embedded in multiply fused or bridged sulfur/carbon/nitrogen rings, with fluorinated positions and a sulfur-linked fluorohydroxymethyl substituent. Sulfur often carries multiple nonoxygen bonds at ring junctions, and some rings contain sulfur bearing hydrogen. Seed 2 produces different sulfur cages bearing carbonyl or aldehyde groups and an amidine-like substituent with a nitrogen-fluorine bond. These structures have abundant rings but little resemblance to a straightforward series of ordinary small-molecule building blocks. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 1.0, aromatic_atom_rate 0.719, mean_smiles_length 61.7 and charged_rate 0.0. Many configurational alternatives are possible but none is explicitly specified. The prior seed-0 best, 0.48118636011729826, was already an unusual fluorinated sulfur cage. The new upper family raises the recorded best while remaining within similarly problematic chemistry.
liabilities: Multiple unusual sulfur-carbon and sulfur-sulfur bonding environments are incorporated into densely fused cages. Formal neutrality does not make these conventional sulfides, sulfoxides or sulfones.
Very short closures and multiply bridged topology create substantial geometry and synthesis concerns; the generated strings do not establish accessible stereoisomers.

Nitrogen-fluorine bonds, fluorinated hydroxyalkyl sulfides, aldehydes and sulfur-chlorine-containing acyl substituents occur in the cited families, adding reactive chemistry to an already demanding framework.
missing_features: Stable, ordinarily bonded implementations of the useful carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated arrangement are missing from the supplied high tail, which is dominated by sulfur cages.
Chemically credible alternative cores with less constrained ring connectivity are not demonstrated at the leading score level. The observed values do not identify a uniquely required ring system.
Defined configuration at the many saturated and sulfur-containing ring junctions is absent, leaving the actual three-dimensional molecular structures underdetermined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated sulfur cage containing the nitrogen dicarbonyl unit scores 0.5903526424693334. Closely related condensed structures score 0.55705130532462 and 0.5527071687189122. A related dicarbonyl cage scores 0.519850349488241, while replacing a carbonyl with an imine-like group in that family gives 0.48440391849409126. This supports the local carbonyl arrangement, but not a general preference for sulfur count or cage complexity. A ring-expanded initial dicarbonyl derivative scores 7.590554525032884e-10, while an already sulfur-rich but differently connected polycycle scores 1.0546805269255595e-09. In seed 2, a late aldehyde-containing cage scores 0.4484554129767839, whereas related structures with altered ring/linker or acyl-sulfur chemistry score 0.004199910554494925 and 0.01685401516576383. The pooled median is 0.074669. The gradient is sensitive to whole-molecule topology and polar-group placement within these cages; it does not demonstrate that their unusual sulfur bonding is synthetically viable or uniquely required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high tails include sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds, tetravalent ring sulfur and densely fused sulfur cages despite charged_rate 0.0 in every proposal set. A bridged nitrogen/carbonyl structure and its unusual sulfur-for-nitrogen analogue both score 0.1996542320706886, while the leading member of that family contains no sulfur. Other cited leaders are ordinary thiol-containing aryl amides, showing that conventional and unusual sulfur chemistry coexist.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently keep sulfur substitutions within chemically credible functional-group and ring-bonding contexts.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treat sulfur coordination, oxidation state and surrounding connectivity as a complete chemical unit when making substitutions. Provide ordinary carbon/nitrogen/oxygen ring alternatives and conventional sulfur functional groups that preserve useful molecular relationships, rather than assuming a neutral, parsable sulfur replacement is chemically credible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimizer set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules include bridged lactam-rich systems, short heterocyclic closures, fluorinated saturated centres and dense sulfur cages with many potential configurational alternatives. Additional cyclization can move a 0.6092182584436399 family to a structure scoring 0.5756365894774199; ring richness alone does not preserve favourable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output supplies abundant ring closures without consistent control of feasible topology, configuration and molecular geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring contraction, expansion and bridging changes with explicit geometric and stereochemical alternatives and chemically credible junctions. Maintain access to simpler constrained structures with the same useful polar relationships. The present evidence establishes incomplete geometric representation, not a demonstrated benefit from any particular configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading aryl amide scores 0.39905049777278273 while its phenyl thioester counterpart scores 0.35659046617209134. In another high family, a methylene-linked amino/sulfur-ring arrangement scores 0.8663008496126992, but shortening the connection to direct nitrogen-sulfur attachment gives 0.3331237338421948. Adding an extra aminomethyl group also does not exceed the corresponding methyl-substituted leader. These observations show that heteroatom abundance is not an adequate account of the useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group attachment context is not reliably conserved when changing amines, amides and aromatic linkers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent amide, amine and linker alternatives while retaining the placement and electronic environment of donors, acceptors and aromatic groups. Distinguish ordinary carbon-linked amines from sulfur-linked or oxygen-linked nitrogen and let accepted feedback assess those specific chemical changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied upper families repeatedly revisit indole carboxamides, elaborated nitrogen dicarbonyl cores, sulfur-rich aryl amine systems, bridged lactam-like structures and closely related sulfur cages. Several large polyene/acetal relatives share 0.6092182584436399 despite changing peripheral unsaturation or oxygen/sulfur substitution. The repeated families and score ties provide limited evidence of independent useful core exploration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically credible scaffold coverage is narrower than the number of local ring, sulfur and peripheral-substituent variants suggests.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to distinct accepted core families and support scaffold replacements or coherent simplifications that preserve useful polar and aromatic relationships. Assess diversity through those relationships and plausible core chemistry, alongside local analogues, rather than relying on a new closure, sulfur atom or substituent as evidence of broad coverage.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
